evidence.reason: At the current tip, `recorder.append(...)` is executed immediately after `Popen()` and outside the `try` block. If the recorder write raises (for example on an I/O error), `boot()` exits before its termination/wait cleanup is armed, leaving the spawned `systemd-run`/QEMU process running and unreaped. Because the transient scope may not yet be registered, caller-side scope cleanup can also miss it. Wrapping the spawn and record write in the same failure-handling block is a routine correctness repair within existing intended cleanup behavior.
